structured_output.answer: This is a product decision for the project owner. The specs don't settle it, and design.md lists it as an open question. Suggested answer: count units, meaning the sum of the quantities across line items. That matches how the cart page already counts items ("Items: N" is the sum of quantities), so a cart showing "Items: 10" would get the discount. The scenarios ("10 items at 2.50 each") work under either reading: the subtotal is 25.00 either way, so they don't decide it. Ask the owner to confirm before implementing task 1.1.

citations.quote: The cart page SHALL show the sum of the quantities of its line items in an element with `data-testid="item-count"`, as the text `Items: N`.
citations.claim: The cart page shows a cart's item count as the sum of its line-item quantities.

structured_output.rationale: The bulk-discount spec says "at least 10 items" but never defines what counts as an item. Its scenarios work under either reading: 10 lines of quantity 1 and one line of quantity 10 both give a subtotal of 25.00 and a discount of 2.50. design.md lists this as an open question, so the owner hasn't decided yet. Which carts qualify is a business rule, so this is a product question. The cart-page spec already counts items as the sum of quantities, which is why I suggest counting units: shoppers would see a count that matches when they qualify.
